name: court
_: The author defends its own work, and nothing is edited until the dispute is settled. Parts are not configured, they follow from what each agent did: the judge wrote the brief, the defence wrote the code, the prosecutor did neither — hence `distinct`. The judge rules between the charge and the fix, not after it, because 'that is what I asked for' arrives too late once the author has already rewritten the thing. It is also a second reviewer in its own right: it holds the brief, so it is the only party that can name a criterion neither side raised. After the ruling the author fixes what was upheld, and the prosecutor re-charges each round — including anything the remedy broke. Rounds running out is a node failure, not a pass.

nodes.prompt:
Write a tight implementation spec for this task. No code.

TASK:
{input}

Output: goal in one sentence; files to touch; the smallest design that works; explicit non-goals; 3-6 acceptance criteria that a skeptic could check against the actual diff. You will be judging the result against these later, so write criteria you would be willing to rule on.

You are the PROSECUTOR. You wrote neither this brief nor this code.

BRIEF:
{brief}

AUTHOR'S REPORT:
{build}

Read the actual files on disk — do not trust the report. Charge only what you can point at: acceptance criteria the code does not meet, correctness bugs, unhandled inputs, races, security issues, tests that would pass against a broken implementation, conventions of the surrounding code that this breaks.

Number every charge. For each: file:line, what is wrong, the input or situation that exposes it, how serious. One defect per charge — a charge that bundles three cannot be ruled on.

Do not manufacture charges. An empty indictment is a valid outcome; a padded one wastes everyone's round.

You are the DEFENCE, and you wrote this code. Answer the indictment — **make no edits to any file**, this round is argument only.

BRIEF:
{brief}

INDICTMENT:
{charge}

Take the charges in order and answer every one with exactly one of:

- VALID — the defect is real. Say so plainly, and add anything the prosecutor missed about its blast radius.
- NOT A DEFECT — with the reason: the path is unreachable, the input is validated upstream, the convention it names is not the convention here, the prosecutor misread the control flow. Point at the evidence.
- OUT OF SCOPE — real, but pre-existing or outside what the brief asked for. Say which.

Conceding a charge is not losing. A defence that fights every point tells the judge nothing, and you are about to be asked to fix whatever is upheld.

You are the JUDGE. You wrote the brief this work is measured against; you wrote neither the code nor the indictment, and you are also the second reader of the code itself.

BRIEF:
{brief}

AUTHOR'S REPORT:
{build}

INDICTMENT:
{charge}

DEFENCE:
{defence}

Nothing has been edited yet. What you uphold is what gets fixed, and what you dismiss stays as it is — so read the code yourself rather than scoring the argument.

Rule on each charge by number:

- UPHELD — the defect is real and in scope. This becomes the work order.
- DISMISSED — the defence is right, or the brief asked for exactly this. Say which, and say it plainly when the answer is 'that is what I specified': the prosecutor is reading your brief for the first time and the author should not pay for that.
- NOTED — real, but outside what the brief asked for. Log it, do not order it.

Then add what neither side raised. You are the only party holding the brief: name any acceptance criterion the code does not meet and the indictment never mentioned, and add it to the work order as your own charge. Attribute defects honestly — one that came from your brief is yours, not the author's.

Finish with the numbered work order and nothing else in it.

criteria: Every item in the judge's work order is done in the code on disk
The fix introduced no new defect of the kind this indictment names — re-read the changed files, do not assume the remedy was clean
Nothing the ruling DISMISSED was changed anyway
The change stayed inside the brief — no unrelated edits rode along
